name: DHC-1 Chipmunk
summary: The RAF's primary trainer for decades, a small, elegant tailwheel aerobatic airplane with a Gipsy Major inline engine; popular in the US as a private warbird and aerobatic sport airplane.

wings: Low, cantilever, slightly tapered wing with rounded tips
engines: Inverted inline four-cylinder Gipsy Major with a very slim nose and two-blade propeller
Exhaust stubs visible low on the cowl
fuselage: Long, sliding bubble canopy covering two seats in tandem
Fixed conventional gear with wide-track main legs
Slender metal fuselage with a pronounced hump behind the canopy
tail: Rounded fin with a moderate sweep
Braced horizontal tail with a sloped line

tellTales: Slim inline-engine nose and a long bubble canopy on a tiny tailwheel trainer
Fixed wide-spaced main gear on a low-wing, tandem two-seater
Rounded, light-airplane silhouette with a gently tapered wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The T-34 is a larger airplane with a flat-six cowl and retractable-looking, higher-stance gear on later models; the Chipmunk is small with a slim inline nose and fixed gear.
The Bulldog has side-by-side seats and a short nose with tricycle gear; the Chipmunk has tandem seats and a tailwheel.
The Stampe is a biplane; the Chipmunk is a low-wing monoplane.
The Pitts is a tiny biplane; the Chipmunk is a monoplane with a bubble canopy.
